claims.statement: > **Quick answer:** If you are researching how to get oral GLP-1 medicines, start with a clinician, identify the exact prescription product, then confirm coverage and pharmacy fulfilment. Wegovy tablets, Foundayo and diabetes-labeled semaglutide tablets have different indications and instructions. An online consultation or advertised price does not establish personal eligibility. [S15][S16][S17][S4]

The current manufacturer-hosted US labels describe several oral products. Wegovy tablets contain semaglutide. Foundayo tablets contain orforglipron. The combined diabetes prescribing information covers Rybelsus and Ozempic tablets, which also contain semaglutide. These names do not establish identical indications, strengths or administration instructions. **Section 1 of each label; Foundayo section 11.** [S15][S16][S17]

| Wegovy tablets | With a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity, the tablets are indicated for long-term weight reduction in adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one weight-related condition; a separate indication concerns major cardiovascular events in adults with established cardiovascular disease and obesity or overweight. Section 1, physical page 3. [S15] |

| Foundayo tablets | With a reduced-calorie diet and increased physical activity, the label describes long-term weight reduction in adults with obesity, or overweight with at least one weight-related condition. This is the orforglipron product, not semaglutide. Section 1, physical page 3; section 11. [S17] |

| Rybelsus and Ozempic tablets | Their combined label describes glycemic control with diet and exercise in adults with type 2 diabetes, and reduction of major cardiovascular events in adults with type 2 diabetes at high risk for those events. Section 1, physical page 3. [S16] |

Ask the clinician to write down the product name and formulation when discussing options. “Ozempic” without the word tablet or injection can leave a practical ambiguity; the current combined tablet label explicitly distinguishes tablets from injections. It also states that Rybelsus and Ozempic tablets are not substitutable on a milligram-for-milligram basis. Do not convert between them using the number printed on a package. **Combined tablet label, sections 2.1 and 2.4.** [S16]

Wegovy's combined label likewise separates tablet and injection indications. Its injection section includes pediatric and liver-disease indications that are not repeated in the tablet indication section. A general page about the brand can therefore be too broad for an oral-product question. Ask which exact formulation and indication the clinician is discussing. **Wegovy label, section 1.** [S15]

Wegovy's official access page describes three practical stages: talk to a doctor, investigate savings and fill the prescription. It explicitly states that Wegovy requires a prescription and points readers toward both in-person and telehealth care resources. Those resources are navigation options, not an independent assessment by Clinic Scout of any listed service. [S4]

Yale Medicine's access overview says patients can begin with a primary care clinician, an obesity-medicine specialist or, in some cases, a telehealth provider. It emphasizes experience and follow-up over time. That supports asking about continuity of care rather than choosing solely by the shortest advertised appointment time. It does not establish the licensing, availability or quality of a particular online provider. [S6]

Prepare a private medication list and questions for the clinical appointment, including other prescriptions, supplements and relevant medical history. The labels describe interactions and contraindications that require product-specific assessment. For example, the semaglutide labels discuss possible effects on other oral medicines, while Foundayo's label also identifies specific drug-interaction categories. **Section 7 of each label.** [S18][S19][S20]

An oral formulation does not remove the need for a clinical risk review. Wegovy and the Rybelsus/Ozempic tablet label contain boxed warnings about thyroid C-cell tumors observed with semaglutide in rodents, with human relevance not determined. They list personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma and MEN 2 among contraindications, alongside the specified hypersensitivity restrictions. **Boxed warnings and section 4.** [S15][S16]

Foundayo also has a boxed warning and contraindications involving personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma and MEN 2. Its warning is not identical to semaglutide's: it explains that orforglipron is not pharmacologically active in rats or mice and did not produce tumors in rodents, while the human relevance of GLP-1-receptor-dependent rodent findings remains undetermined. Avoid collapsing those distinct label statements into one claim about all drugs. **Foundayo boxed warning and section 4.** [S17]

The labels also describe significant gastrointestinal, pancreatic, gallbladder, kidney, hypoglycemia and hypersensitivity risks or precautions, with product-specific wording. These summaries are not the complete safety information and do not determine whether a reader can take a medicine. Ask the clinician to review the complete current label and explain which warnings are relevant to your history. **Section 5 of each label.** [S18][S19][S20]

Pregnancy, breastfeeding, planned procedures and other medicines belong in that conversation. The labels contain different reproductive and procedural precautions; they should not be compressed into a universal instruction about stopping, switching or timing medicines. We do not provide an individualized plan for any of those situations. **Sections 5, 7 and 8 of each label.** [S18][S19][S20]

A contraindication is not the same heading as a warning or precaution. For example, the labels place personal or family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma and MEN 2 in the contraindications section, while discussing several other conditions under warnings and precautions. A comparison article should not silently move a condition between those categories or replace the named thyroid-cancer type with every possible thyroid diagnosis. **Sections 4 and 5 of each label.** [S15][S16][S17]

NovoCare Pharmacy's published Wegovy-tablet self-pay prices were **checked 2026-10-09**. The amounts below are medication prices for the stated tablet strength and supply, not a personal quote or total care cost. [S5]

For a savings offer, check the official product-specific terms separately from the self-pay prices above. NovoCare's page distinguishes insurance and self-pay pathways; these payment routes do not have interchangeable conditions. [S5]

The official Wegovy access page describes filling a prescription through a local pharmacy or using delivery, subject to terms. NovoCare's pharmacy page describes having the prescriber send the prescription and looking for a confirmation message. These are reported fulfilment pathways, not proof that a particular pharmacy has your product available or that a shipment has been approved. [S4][S5]

The current Rybelsus/Ozempic tablet label expressly warns against milligram-for-milligram substitution. Wegovy's label has separate tablet and injection instructions. These are concrete reasons not to infer a replacement regimen from a similar active ingredient or a similar number on a box. **Section 2.1; Wegovy section 2.5.** [S15][S16]

The labels differ in how tablets are taken. Wegovy and the Rybelsus/Ozempic tablet label describe morning administration on an empty stomach with water and a waiting period before food, beverages or other oral medicines. Foundayo's label describes once-daily use with or without food. These are product-label distinctions to discuss, not a recommendation to choose one medicine over another. **Section 2.1 of each label.** [S15][S16][S17]

Also ask what follow-up is included, who reviews tolerability or other concerns, and how a future change in insurance or supply would be handled. Yale Medicine's access overview emphasizes a clinician who can follow the patient over time. That supports planning for communication beyond the first visit; it is not proof that every service provides the same level of support. [S6]

The OASIS 4 randomized, double-blind trial studied oral semaglutide 25 mg against placebo with lifestyle interventions in adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes. At the week-64 assessment, the oral-semaglutide group had greater mean weight reduction, but gastrointestinal adverse events were more common than with placebo. The study was funded by Novo Nordisk. This qualitative result applies to that product, population, comparison and study period; it is not an individual forecast. [S7]

OASIS 1 studied a different oral-semaglutide amount, 50 mg, for 68 weeks in adults without type 2 diabetes and also reported greater weight reduction than placebo alongside more gastrointestinal adverse events. OASIS 2 used 50 mg in an East Asian population with different entry criteria and included participants with type 2 diabetes. Those studies do not turn a 50 mg research regimen into instructions for a currently prescribed product. [S8][S9]

These trials were not a head-to-head comparison of every pill and injection named on this page. Do not rank products by placing percentages from different trials side by side without considering the populations, design and analysis. The captured OASIS 4 registration and protocol identify the planned study; observed outcomes here come from the published original report, not from the mere existence of a registration. [S7][S8][S9][S10]

The official access material says Wegovy requires a prescription, and NovoCare says the products on its pharmacy page require one. Start with a clinical evaluation rather than treating a sales page as a prescription decision. This guide does not endorse sellers offering a shortcut around that process. [S4][S5]

Both contain semaglutide, but the current labels describe different products and indications. Wegovy tablets have adult weight-management and specified cardiovascular indications; the combined Rybelsus/Ozempic tablet label describes type 2 diabetes and its specified cardiovascular population. **Section 1 of both labels.** [S15][S16]

No personal prescription approval is established by this guide. The access pathway begins with a clinician, and the medicine remains prescription-only. Ask the service what an evaluation covers and what happens when the requested medicine is not prescribed; we have not verified a universal refund or outcome policy. [S4]

That conclusion is not established here. The current oral labels contain significant warnings, contraindications and different administration requirements. Discuss the product-specific balance and practical instructions with the clinician rather than inferring safety from the absence of an injection. **Boxed warnings; sections 2.1 and 4.** [S15][S16][S17]

No individual cost is verified here. The manufacturer pharmacy page separates payment routes and attaches conditions to advertised amounts. Ask for the exact supply, product, payment arrangement and next-fill terms, plus any service charges quoted separately. [S5]

The cited trials studied defined regimens and populations; they are not a personal prescribing plan. In particular, the combined Rybelsus/Ozempic tablet label rejects milligram-for-milligram substitution. Take switching or regimen questions to the prescriber and pharmacist. **Combined tablet label, section 2.1.** [S16][S7][S8][S9]
| 1.5 mg | $149 for one bottle of 30 tablets. [S5] |
| 4 mg | $199 for one bottle of 30 tablets. [S5] |
| 9 mg or 25 mg | $299 for one bottle of 30 tablets. [S5] |

Eligibility and restrictions apply. Novo Nordisk reserves the right to modify or cancel the programme at any time. These are the published 2026-10-09 terms, not a guarantee of your next fill; separately quoted consultation, membership or other care charges are not established by this medication-price table. [S5]

Semaglutide binds to and activates the GLP-1 receptor. The diabetes-tablet label describes glucose-dependent insulin stimulation and glucagon reduction, with a minor delay in early post-meal gastric emptying. This explains the mechanism, not an individual's response. **Combined tablet label, section 12.1, physical page 6.** [S12]

Foundayo contains a different active ingredient, orforglipron, whose label also identifies it as a GLP-1 receptor agonist. Sharing a receptor class does not make its instructions or evidence interchangeable with semaglutide tablets. **Foundayo label, section 11 and boxed warning.** [S17]

The combined diabetes label bases Rybelsus and Ozempic-tablet glycemic effectiveness on controlled Rybelsus studies in adults with type 2 diabetes. In its 26-week double-blind randomized monotherapy trial, adults inadequately controlled with diet and exercise received semaglutide tablets or placebo; the 7 mg and 14 mg study groups had statistically significant HbA1c reductions versus placebo. These are diabetes study regimens, not strength-selection, conversion or weight-loss instructions. **Combined tablet label, sections 14.1–14.2, physical page 7.** [S12]

CMS's Medicare GLP-1 Bridge information, checked **2026-10-09**, describes a July 1, 2026–December 31, 2027 demonstration outside ordinary Part D coverage and payment flows. Listed weight-management products include Wegovy tablets and Foundayo. Eligible Part D plan types, clinical criteria, a prescription and prescriber prior authorization are required; Medicare enrollment alone does not establish eligibility. [S13]

CMS directs Part D-covered indications, such as type 2 diabetes, through the Part D plan instead of the Bridge. Identify the oral product, indication and programme together: conditional Bridge access is neither universal oral-GLP-1 coverage nor a manufacturer self-pay offer. [S13]

Wegovy-tablet and Foundayo labels describe reducing excess body weight and maintaining weight reduction long term. They do not establish a universal short course or an individual treatment duration. **Section 1 of both labels.** [S15][S17]

In the STEP 4 randomized withdrawal trial, adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes who reached subcutaneous semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly after a 20-week run-in continued treatment or switched to placebo for 48 weeks, with lifestyle intervention in both groups. Continued treatment produced further average weight loss; the placebo-switch group regained weight. Gastrointestinal events were more frequent with continued treatment. This selected-participant injection trial does not predict how much or how quickly weight returns after stopping oral tablets, or supply individual stopping, restarting or lifelong-treatment instructions. [S14]

sections.heading: About this guide and its limits
paragraphs: **Sources checked October 9, 2026; labels rechecked October 13, 2026.** Clinic Scout is an independent comparison publisher, not a clinic, pharmacy or insurer. We explain the access process and compare reported information; we do not prescribe, decide whether you qualify, or choose a treatment. This page contains no affiliate purchase links and collects no health or contact information. The worksheet below is available on the page, not by email.

The most useful first distinction is between access and treatment suitability. Access questions include who evaluates you, which product is prescribed, how a pharmacy receives the prescription and what a payment quote includes. Treatment questions include whether a medicine is appropriate, which regimen to use and how to monitor it. Take the second group to the prescribing clinician rather than trying to solve it with a comparison table.

Our five checks are a discussion framework, not steps that guarantee approval. You can use them with an existing clinician, a specialist or a telehealth service you independently assess. The purpose is to leave each conversation knowing the next responsible party and what remains unconfirmed.

sections.heading: What oral-semaglutide studies can and cannot tell you
paragraphs: The OASIS 4 randomized, double-blind trial studied oral semaglutide 25 mg against placebo with lifestyle interventions in adults with overweight or obesity without diabetes. At the week-64 assessment, the oral-semaglutide group had greater mean weight reduction, but gastrointestinal adverse events were more common than with placebo. The study was funded by Novo Nordisk. This qualitative result applies to that product, population, comparison and study period; it is not an individual forecast. [S7]

OASIS 1 studied a different oral-semaglutide amount, 50 mg, for 68 weeks in adults without type 2 diabetes and also reported greater weight reduction than placebo alongside more gastrointestinal adverse events. OASIS 2 used 50 mg in an East Asian population with different entry criteria and included participants with type 2 diabetes. Those studies do not turn a 50 mg research regimen into instructions for a currently prescribed product. [S8][S9]

These trials were not a head-to-head comparison of every pill and injection named on this page. Do not rank products by placing percentages from different trials side by side without considering the populations, design and analysis. The captured OASIS 4 registration and protocol identify the planned study; observed outcomes here come from the published original report, not from the mere existence of a registration. [S7][S8][S9][S10]

The evidence also does not establish the performance of a provider, a savings programme or a differently formulated compounded product. We have not retrieved product-matched evidence that would justify transferring these results to those settings. The diabetes-tablet evidence above concerns glycemic control, not these OASIS weight-management outcomes. For cardiovascular effects or a different formulation, use the evidence relevant to the actual treatment rather than extrapolating from a weight-management study.

sections.heading: Your on-page appointment and pharmacy checklist
paragraphs: Use this as a private note for your own conversations, not as information to submit to Clinic Scout. Do not post prescriptions, medical records or insurance identifiers in public comments to obtain an unofficial eligibility answer. We do not operate a patient-support service or verify individual prescriptions.

rows: Exact brand and whether the prescription is for tablets or injections.
Who evaluates suitability and who supplies the treatment instructions.
Insurance or self-pay route, supply period, full quote and unresolved conditions.
Destination pharmacy, confirmation stage and contact for questions.
Clinical contact, what support was described and which questions remain open.

sections.heading: Methodology and update policy
paragraphs: The Clinic Scout Editorial Team checked current manufacturer-hosted US prescribing information, official access and pharmacy pages, and the cited PubMed originals on October 9, 2026, and rechecked the three oral labels on October 13, 2026. We compared the exact-query search results for reader questions, not for medical authority. The original physical PDF pages were inspected before parsing; label page references above refer to those original documents, not a renumbered extract.

Our [editorial guidelines](/editorial-guidelines/) explain organization-only attribution and our comparison role. This article is not a medical signoff or a personal eligibility determination. Programme prices, stock, provider availability and individual insurance decisions remain unverified unless expressly stated otherwise; this guide does not quote a personal treatment total.

We will revisit this guide when product labels, official access pathways or programme terms change. That is an update policy, not a claim that future rechecks have happened. Before relying on an instruction or payment offer, return to the current official document and the responsible clinician, pharmacy or insurer. Keep the source date attached when sharing a summary.
